title: Unbatched Write Loops (N+1 Write Amplification)
pattern: Iteratively executing individual, independent database write queries inside a loop instead of batching them into a single bulk write operation.
why_bad: Causes extreme write amplification and network overhead. For every single write, the system pays the penalty of database driver round-trips, parsing overhead, write-ahead logging (WAL) flush-to-disk, and index updates. This is particularly destructive for SSD storage wear and transaction log contention.
detection: Database write commands executing inside loop structures (`for`, `while`, `.iter().for_each()`) without any grouping or batch parameters.
counterexample: Trivial scripts or simple background workers executing a few low-frequency writes where latency is not a concern.
source: *Alex Petrov - Database Internals (2019)*, Chapter 3 & Chapter 5; *Martin Kleppmann - Designing Data-Intensive Applications (2017)*, Chapter 3.
